Aapoph Sovereign Guard.description:
Physically, aapoph sovereign guards tower over other aapophs, but their hulking stature and unquestioning obedience belie an intelligence unique even among the zyss. Despite their cunning, sovereign guards are rarely treacherous or self-serving; rather, each guard is expected to devote their existence solely to the advancement of their superiors. Even when beset on all sides by treacherous political machinations, zyss monarchs implicitly trust their sovereign guards, whose powerful bulk, keen senses, and whirling halberds are more dependable than any shield.

Serpentfolk society is riddled with secret organizations, many of which preserve long-lost traditions from the height of the ancient sekmin empire. Exclusive orders of aapoph sovereign guards and zyss assassins, among others, trace their origins back millennia, training in the same techniques they employed in the days when mammalian humanoids were nothing but servants or prey.

Aapoph Training

The towering aapophs employed as sovereign guards aren't born larger than their siblings. Rather, zyss trainers select certain aapoph hatchlings to be raised as guards. These young aapophs are reared in isolated nurseries where they're trained in advanced weaponcraft. According to rumor, the secret of a sovereign guard's increased cunning and stature lies in a diet regarded as blasphemous even by other sekmins.

Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Ayindilar Occultist.description:
Secretive groups of ayindilar occultists gather to worship otherworldly entities or pursue magics forbidden by their communities at large. Imbuing their weapons with mind-numbing psychic energy and utilizing their occult talents to confuse and confound foes, ayindilar occultists are the root of many of the biases outsiders feel toward their people.

In the days following Earthfall, many elves retreated from Golarion's surface to the gloom of the Darklands, founding city-states throughout the subterranean continents. Over generations, more and more of these sub-surface elves were born with physical colorations that matched the muted hues of their new home, with pale lavender skin and stark white hair eventually becoming the most common ayindilar complexion.

Today, little remains of the ancient ayindilar civilizations. Their great cities lie abandoned, and the underground trade routes they once traveled are now monster-infested tunnels. Ayindilar elves can be encountered throughout the Darklands, but they rarely gather in great numbers or seek attention. Most ayindilars are nomadic, avoiding contact with outsiders as they hunt prey or follow herds of moss-grazing lizards through lightless caverns. Others live in enclaves within larger cities, primarily on Nar-Voth, dwelling in the proverbial shadows cast by more established Darklands societies.

While some elven cultures embrace arcane, divine, or primal traditions, ayindilars are more interested in occult research, and many have learned to channel the psychic energies that permeate the Darklands. The magic practiced by ayindilars tends to be subtle, and their ability to cloud minds and remain hidden from sight has garnered them a reputation as sneaks and tricksters—a notoriety that fuels many ayindilars' own distrust of outsiders. Ironically, this mutual distrust drives some ayindilars to prey on surface folk and Darklands dwellers alike, further solidifying their sinister reputations.

Lost Cities

During their exodus from Golarion's surface, some ayindilar elves traveled through the Darklands all the way to Tian Xia, while others delved deeper toward the vaults of Orv. Most settled on Sekamina, building massive cities throughout. Their greatest city was Zirnakaynin, which legend holds was the birthplace of ayindilar occultism. For reasons unknown, Zirnakaynin fell. The other ayindilar city-states soon followed, and while many of these ruins have been reclaimed by other Darklands societies, lost Zirnakaynin remains mysterious and abandoned.

Cruelty of the Crowd

Today, ayindilar elves avoid congregating in large settlements, distrusting their own leaders nearly as much as they do outsiders. According to ayindilar lore, when more than a few thousand ayindilars gather in one place, their society undergoes sinister changes. Wicked behavior increasingly becomes the norm, as customs and institutions begin to echo those of the crueler ayindilar city-states. It's unclear whether this supposed phenomenon prompted ayindilars to abandon their ancient cities, but it certainly discourages modern ayindilar elves from returning to them.

Corundumite.description:
Corundumites are flying earth elementals that look like faceted red or blue gemstones. Drawn to veins rich with rubies, sapphires, and other precious stones, corundumites regard themselves as the guardians of the earth's riches, attacking those who mine or even examine the uncut gems in their domains. They can be hostile to travelers who have gemstones in their possession, but those who carry no such stones—or who surrender their gems as recompense for the slight—are usually allowed to pass unharmed. Why corundumites are so protective of the stones in their care remains unknown, though those who have spoken with the elementals report that they seem to regard the gems not as symbols of wealth, but rather as living, thinking beings.

Gem Body

When it dies, a corundumite transforms into an inert—and highly valuable—corundum gemstone such as a ruby or sapphire. An intact gemstone harvested from a dead corundumite can be worth as much as 2,000 gp, provided it's in good condition. Unfortunately, not every battle leaves behind a perfectly preserved gemstone. If the damage that reduced the corundumite to 0 Hit Points was bludgeoning, force, or sonic damage, the gem smashes into 2d6 fragments, each of which is worth only 100 gp.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and immune to vision of doom for 24 hours.

8DQHdcBWilzBI5Z3.name: Vision of Doom

Losing a head doesn't kill a chimera (as long as it has at least one head left), but it does prevent it from making Strikes with the lost head or using any abilities granted by the head.
BvW0oiNlKIAxOPrr.name: Three-Headed

M8CbYRKihCNDpNGI.description: Doomcrier's magma worm head exhales a blast of flame in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] that deals @Damage[16d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:36|basic|options:area-effect] save). M8CbYRKihCNDpNGI.name: Fire Breath

ipu2uvrrUMZRvNwP.name: Three-Headed Strike

kixUx73oj09Sr7fh.description: Doomcrier's thunderbird head blasts its foes with peals of thunder and crackling bolts of lightning. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] takes @Damage[8d6[electricity],8d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:36|basic] save). kixUx73oj09Sr7fh.name: Storm Blast

Dragonfire Fly.description:
A dragonfire fly is an immense dragonfly with wings veined in delicate traceries of red fire. Its faceted eyes are huge gemstones that blaze with internal luminescence. While on the hunt, the dragonfire fly zips through subterranean labyrinths or clings silently to cavern walls, lancing prey with solid jets of flame cast from its eyes.

Although dragonfire flies most often use fire to catch their food, they adapt readily to their enemies' weapons and defenses. When magic harms a dragonfire fly, the fly's eyes and the flames across its wings change color, burning with white frost, yellow electricity, or whatever other energy it was exposed to. This same energy burns in the dragonfire fly's eye rays.

Opal Eyes

If a dragonfire fly’s eyes resemble gems, it’s because they are! Both of a dragonfire fly’s multifaceted eyes are immense, translucent opals as large as a human head. The gems change hue when the fly’s flame takes on a new color, and they retain this color when the dragonfire fly dies. Each of the fly’s eyes is worth at least 10,000 gold—if a buyer for such a large single stone can be found.

9dsUUsPfwwoqXtzz.description: The fly can Fly at half Speed while it has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} in its mandibles, carrying that creature along with it.
9dsUUsPfwwoqXtzz.name: Carry

PzbRWml1pY151w3l.description: 30 feet. The aura sheds dim light of the same color as the fly's current fire wings color.
PzbRWml1pY151w3l.name: Firelight

i8dZjb5pFGRrZsaX.description:
Trigger While Flying, the dragonfire fly is hit by a ranged Strike that deals physical damage

Effect The fly spins in flight, deflecting some of the force of the attack. The fly gains resistance 15 to physical damage from the triggering attack.
i8dZjb5pFGRrZsaX.name: Barrel Roll

yPK80D4ILDtdCSAz.description:
When the fly is first encountered, the fly's wings burn with red flame. When the fly takes acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, or void damage, the fly's wing flame color changes depending on the type of damage dealt. If an attack or effect deals more than one of these damage types, the fly chooses which damage type affects their fire wings color. The fly gains resistance 15 to the damage type associated with its new fire wings color, and its eye beam ranged Strike deals that damage type. After 1 minute, the fly's fire wings revert to red flame. The damage type, fire color, and other effects of each fire wings color are:

Acid: Green fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes @Damage[3d6[persistent,acid]] damage.

Cold: White fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes a –15-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

Electricity: Yellow fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round.

Fire: Red fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes @Damage[6d6[fire]] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:32|basic] save.

Sonic: Purple fire. The fly emits a loud buzz. A creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} while in the fly's firelight aura.

Void: Black fire. The fly becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} and loses its firelight aura until its Fire Wings change to a different color.
yPK80D4ILDtdCSAz.name: Fire Wings

Dragonfire Fly.name: Dragonfire Fly

JMqabFSfAqxqFXdu.description: When the dream cradle is destroyed, the egg-balloon shatters, releasing a cloud of nightmarish oneiric energy. Creatures other than the pilot and passengers within 30 feet of the dream cradle take @Damage[14d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:32|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:fleeing,inflicts:frightened] save). On a failed save, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round on a critical failure). The dream cradle then uses that last of its magical reserves to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.A2JfEKe6BZcTG1S8]{Fly} on the pilot and each passenger.
JMqabFSfAqxqFXdu.name: Burst

WIFfax9ZqFa52zHK.description: The dream cradle's Speed doubles while moving straight up or down
WIFfax9ZqFa52zHK.name: Vertical Travel

bKpTXAvtrIxljgg2.description: Each day, the dream cradle can be used for up to 1 hour before it shrinks back into its egg form to recharge for 8 hours. One minute before it shrinks, the balloon wobbles in warning, giving the pilot time to land.
bKpTXAvtrIxljgg2.name: Recharge

EE2BgcGPaSE7LkJp.name: Truesight (Constant)

d1M5TxafdFoOywtm.name: Rejuvenation

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. Eroded Vault Lifter.description:
Vault lifters are sentient stone constructs roughly carved into the semblance of giant xiomorns. Each vault lifter is encircled by a spinning ring, called a rotor, which grants the lifter the ability to fly.

Xiomorns created vault lifters to help construct their vaults throughout the Plane of Earth and across the Universe. With the ability to airlift heavy burdens and possessed with enough intelligence to carry out complex instructions, vault lifters were valuable lieutenants in the xiomorns' vast terraforming projects. Vault lifters were intended to be more than simple laborers, however; they were also built as weapons of war. In combat, vault lifters spin their rotors into fearsome buzz saws capable of propelling them at high speeds and slicing foes in half.

Abandoned Guardians

While some vault lifters continue to serve living xiomorns, others have been left behind in long-abandoned locations. Over the years, many of these forgotten vault lifters have completed their assignments and deactivated themselves. Others continue to perform some unending task, such as "keep this area clean," "prevent unauthorized entry," or "I'll be back in a bit—wait for my return." After millennia spent in solitude, some abandoned vault lifters become fanatical about their final orders, spinning them into complex philosophical systems heavy with moral significance.

GC5YbcsuLKeA2T9Y.description:
Requirements The vault lifter's rotor is activated

Effect The lifter Flies up to three times its Fly Speed in a straight line without triggering reactions. At the end of this flight, the lifter must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] saving throw. On a failure, the lifter's rotor is deactivated.
GC5YbcsuLKeA2T9Y.name: Overdrive

IWfz9CXXr3A4SL05.description: The vault lifter attempts to [[/act reposition]] a creature it has @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, moving the creature into a space adjacent to it. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the lifter's multiple attack penalty.
IWfz9CXXr3A4SL05.name: Draw In

l6NRWWaC6EmEx9sp.description: A vault lifter can Fly at half Speed while it has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, carrying that creature along with it.
l6NRWWaC6EmEx9sp.name: Carry

sdXO1sq7jTiI9LHD.description: These vault lifters have been partially reclaimed by the elements. At the start of an encounter, the lifter is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} until the end of its first turn.
sdXO1sq7jTiI9LHD.name: Overgrown

vFe36uIHulZ5o7yY.description:
The vault lifter's rotor spins, becoming a buzzing blur. While the rotor is activated, the lifter gains a fly Speed of 40 feet. The spinning rotor also creates an aura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] around the lifter. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:34|options:damaging-effect,forced-movement,inflicts:prone] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected, and the vault lifter's rotor is deactivated. The lifter loses its fly Speed and aura until it Activates Rotor again.

Success The creature takes @Damage[2d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[4d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage. If the creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the vault lifter, they are pushed back 15 feet and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
vFe36uIHulZ5o7yY.name: Activate Rotor

Etumult.description:
In ancient times, a cabal of primalists imbued an amalgam of beasts with both supernatural might and a hatred of magic itself, hoping to achieve a potent weapon for use against arcane spellcasters. Effective beyond expectation, the first leydroths broke free and turned on their creators. Worse, the leydroths bred true, and these reclusive predators have long outlived their original creators.

Leydroths look like distorted, apelike felines with many-branching horns growing from the backs of their heads. Their thickly muscled limbs end in glowing claws.

BNtTt4rbMDmj6cYA.description: You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. Attempt a counteract check against the target. If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.
BNtTt4rbMDmj6cYA.name: Dispel Magic (At Will)

Ixt0Bpsg2FgwTGiy.description:
The leydroth unleashes a bestial roar that reverberates within a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. It rolls an Intimidation check and compares the result to the Will DC of each creature in the area, with the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize}.

It also uses this result to attempt to counteract each spell or magical effect in the area, plus one item or effect on each creature in the area, with the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic}.

The leydroth can't use Dispelling Roar again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Dispelling Roar]]{1d4 rounds}.
Ixt0Bpsg2FgwTGiy.name: Dispelling Roar

OlwLivQfLQIh0ut7.description: The leydroth detects the source and school of each source of magic within 60 feet as an imprecise sense.
OlwLivQfLQIh0ut7.name: Magic Sense

Q3683RHwk5skFzWi.description:
Frequency once per round

Trigger The leydroth hits a creature, object, or spell effect with a Strike

Q3683RHwk5skFzWi.name: Dispelling Strike

fKqimVsLOPsE2xN0.description:
Trigger A creature within 60 feet Casts a Spell

fKqimVsLOPsE2xN0.name: Menace to Magic

Facetal Branch.description:
Facetal branches are elder facetals whose gemstone bodies have grown into large glowing crystals. Instead of donning humanoid guises as facetal nodes do, facetal branches use hardlight to project insect-like bodies in the image of their deity, Sairazul.

With minds capable of revisiting their memories with crystalline perfection, facetal branches can both move and communicate across space and time. They're named after the constant improvements they make to their past selves, navigating branches of alternate histories to achieve crystalline perfection.

Gathering Moss

While their younger cousins, facetal nodes, travel to accumulate knowledge, facetal branches turn their explorations inwards, scrutinizing past actions for minor imperfections that could stunt their slow, crystalline growth. When they identify a flaw, they can reach backwards in time to alter their past—but only if their past self occupies the same location as their present one. For this reason, facetal branches tend to stay put.

Ck7FqLoWoPJEqEcY.description: 30 feet. The facetal branch's glowing gem fills the area of the aura with bright light. The branch can deactivate or activate its aura as a single action with the concentrate trait.
Ck7FqLoWoPJEqEcY.name: Luminescent Aura

PgK6G5QsHGnCu9S6.description: The node projects a new Huge, insect-like form around itself, changing its appearance but not its statistics. The node's projected form is a solid body made of hardlight. While using a projected form, the node's true form, a Tiny gem, is always visible embedded in the projection's abdomen or thorax. The gemstone is the facetal's sensory organ, and if the gemstone is covered, the facetal node is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded}.
PgK6G5QsHGnCu9S6.name: Hardlight Projection

auhwjjdCoiNL3vhY.description: On a critical hit with a gem ray Strike, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.
auhwjjdCoiNL3vhY.name: Blinding Attack

ewjz8tvV71Xwlpnu.description:
When a facetal node is reduced to 0 Hit Points, their hardlight body is destroyed, leaving behind the node's true form, a Tiny glowing gemstone. In this form, the node's Speed is 0, they're immune to damage, and they're deactivated. While deactivated, they can't take actions or speak, although they can use telepathy. The node remains deactivated until it reactivates at a time determined by the GM (usually after decades or more).

While deactivated, the facetal branch can't use temporal telepathy, and their luminescent aura is deactivated.

hsC0LEx2Tmu5vJBx.name: Blinking Strobe

sxok5nxYyO5B12Xw.description: The facetal branch can communicate telepathically with themselves at a specific moment in the past, provided their past self occupies the branch's current space.
sxok5nxYyO5B12Xw.name: Temporal Telepathy

xFKazim15tV9Jn1H.description:
The facetal branch can pluck creatures from the very flow of time. One creature the branch can see within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save. The branch can target themself, automatically failing their save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Temporal Skip for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Failure The creature winks out of existence for 1 round (or for up to 1 hour if the branch targeted themself). Until the creature reappears, time doesn't pass for the creature. When the effect ends, the creature returns to the space it occupied when it disappeared or to the nearest space if the original is now filled.
xFKazim15tV9Jn1H.name: Temporal Skip

Facetal Node.description:
Facetal nodes are the youngest facetals, having lived for mere tens of thousands of years. Though nearly eternal from the viewpoint of mortals, nodes measure their lives on a geological time scale, regarding themselves as neophytes compared to elder facetals and other immortal elementals. Most facetal nodes travel far and wide to gather knowledge, using their projected humanoid bodies to blend in among other sentient beings. They tend to observe the affairs of mortals impassively, unmoved by hardships which, from their perspective, last no longer than the blink of an eye.

Formed under immense geological pressure over untold eons, facetals are intelligent, eloquent elemental gemstones. While facetals can’t affect the world in their true gem forms, they can focus their inner radiance to create corporeal bodies made of hardlight.

Everpresent Gem

No matter what form they project to the world, a facetal node's true body—their gem—is always visible somewhere on their hardlight body. Since a facetal node senses the world through this gemstone, they often go to great pains to hide the stone's significance, disguising it as an ordinary piece of jewelry, the crystal on the tip of a walking staff, or some other mundane jewel. A facetal's gem is functionally unbreakable, requiring the will of a god or similar force to shatter it.

General Vesperix.description:
Xiomorn troopers are an elite military force formed from the ranks of xiomorn vault keepers. Armed with technology only they understand, xiomorn troopers hold the line against those who oppose the mysterious aims of the vault builders.

Many xiomorn troopers possess special training or equipment that helps them perform specific roles within their strike force. Comm troopers, for example, can communicate telepathically with their fellow troopers, while scout troopers surround themselves with fields of light-bending energy on their patrols. The batons of shock troopers carry charges of electricity that they use to stun their foes, while rad troopers are armed with explosives that release bursts of a sickening radiation, to which the troopers themselves are immune.

Mysterious Generals

Some xiomorn troopers consider themselves part of a single military organization led by a figure whose identity is unknown even to the highest-ranking troopers. Referred to only as the "Commander," this mysterious leader hands down orders along an extended, telepathic chain of command. In many Orvian vaults, the Commander is presumed to be a vault builder—or perhaps a fellow trooper in direct contact with the builders—though some troopers insist the Commander is simply an imaginary figurehead created to inspire loyalty. The fact that different squads of troopers have at times been given conflicting orders lends credence to the latter belief.

HEdMnQyDHhWSuXDf.name: Crystal Detonation

YNrcQ6ke19OFZzsS.description: The trooper Steps and makes a melee Strike. Up to two other xiomorn troopers within 15 feet can Step as a reaction.
YNrcQ6ke19OFZzsS.name: Fighting Formation

hOkfh02TI5JUhAw5.description: After the xiomorn trooper deals damage with a crystal shard Strike, a glowing green crystal embeds itself in the target's body. The crystal sheds dim light for 10 feet. While a creature has at least one crystal embedded in its body, all xiomorn troopers gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [[/act seek]] the creature and to Survival checks to [[/act track]] the creature. In addition, all xiomorn troopers gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the creature. A creature can Interact to remove all tracking crystals embedded in themselves or an adjacent creature.
hOkfh02TI5JUhAw5.name: Tracking Crystal

A roiling incant is as much a mass of unstable magic as it is a creature. Is isn't living or undead, nor is it even a construct. Each time a roiling incant casts one of its non-cantrip spells, it drains its own magic to do so, taking @Damage[5[force]] damage.

You shape a wall of solid stone. You create a 1-inch-thick wall of stone up to 120 feet long, and 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically, so you can use it to form a bridge or set of stairs, for example. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 14, and 50 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section of the wall can be moved through, but the rubble created from it is difficult terrain.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 15.

On a critical hit, double the initial damage, but not the splash damage, and the target you hit must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw or fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

psQx9S2R7lSArofa.name: Exploding Earth (At Will)

You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Knucklehead.description:
Knuckleheads are fleshwarps named after the oversized hand that sprouts from their neck in place of a skull. Their dangling, armor-plated arms are equally disproportionate, even in comparison to their massive frames, which range in size from 10 to 14 feet tall. Knuckleheads can use their arms either as a second pair of legs or to deliver stone-shattering punches. They feed by crushing a victim in their head-hand, the palm of which is split by a toothy maw.

It's often said that encountering a fleshwarp is evidence there's an even greater monster nearby: the cruel being that tortured the fleshwarp into its distorted form. The Darklands are home to many such monsters, both the fleshwarps and their creators.

Failed Experiments

Knuckleheads are the product of an effort to turn prisoners into obedient servants, but it turns out that a brain isn't an optional luxury when creating the perfect laborer. Driven by hunger and blind instinct, knuckleheads hunted their creators and fellow prisoners alike. Now that they've escaped into the Darklands, they prowl pitch-black caverns, attracted by the smell of flesh.

Monofilamental.description:
A monofilamental is a floating bubble made of glowing, crystalline strands. From this complex web of interconnected threads, a highly ordered intelligence emerges, one capable of turning each of its delicate skeins into an unbreakable, serrating lash.

Drifting through the Darklands on subterranean air currents, a monofilamental looks as delicate as a soap bubble or spider web. In fact, the psychic intelligence that animates the monofilamental exerts an unbreakable mental control over each of its strands, granting them unrivaled tensile strength. A single monofilamental thread can slice through steel or stone, to say nothing of the flesh and bone toward which the construct unerringly drifts. If monofilamental thread could be harvested, it would both be a powerful tool and a fearsome weapon; when a monofilamental dies, however, so too does the mental force that fortifies each thread.

Collective Network

Although intelligent, monofilamentals are spun by—and exist only to serve—a species of non-sapient spiders native to the Plane of Earth. Working collectively through instinct, clusters of these extraplanar spiders spin webs of unmatched complexity, some of which awaken to sentience as monofilamentals. Once created, a monofilamental bends its brilliant psychic intellect toward a narrow purpose: fetching meat for its arachnid creators.

Fz7dV6sAH9G42uFF.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.
Fz7dV6sAH9G42uFF.name: Interplanar Teleport (To Plane of Earth or the Universe Only)

You transform the target into an undead creature with a level up to that allowed in the Creature Creation Rituals table. There are many versions of this ritual, each specific to a particular type of undead (one ritual for all zombies, one for skeletons, one for ghouls, and so on), and the rituals that create rare undead are also rare. Some forms of undead, such as liches, form using their own unique methods and can't be created with a version of create undead.

Critical Success The target becomes an undead creature of the appropriate type. If it's at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion. This gives it the minion trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you command it, and commanding it is a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits. You can have a maximum of four minions under your control. If it's intelligent and doesn't become a minion, the undead is helpful to you for awakening it, though it's still a horrid and evil creature. If it's unintelligent and doesn't become a minion, you can give it one simple command. It pursues that goal single-mindedly, ignoring any of your subsequent commands.

Success As critical success, except an intelligent undead that doesn't become your minion is only friendly to you, and an unintelligent undead that doesn't become your minion leaves you alone unless you attack it. It marauds the local area rather than following your command.

Failure You fail to create the undead.

Critical Failure You create the undead, but its soul, tortured by your foul necromancy, is full of nothing but hatred for you. It attempts to destroy you.

cN0uSsE4bDqglpcP.description:
You craft an imaginary scene that includes up to 10 discrete creatures or objects of various sizes, all of which must be within the spell's area. These elements generate appropriate sounds and smells, and they feel right to the touch. Elements of an illusory scene are incapable of speech. Unlike with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.f8SBoXiXQjlCKqly]{Illusory Creature} spell, creatures in your scene lack combat abilities and statistics. Your scene doesn't include changes to the environment around it, though you can place your scene within the illusory environment of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HBJPsonQnWcC3qdX]{Mirage} spell.

When you create the scene, you can choose to have it be static or follow a program. Though a static scene is stationary, it includes basic natural movement. For example, wind blowing on an illusory piece of paper would rustle it. A program can be up to 1 minute long and repeats when finished. For instance, you could create a scene of two orcs fighting each other, and the fight would go the same way for each repetition. If you create a loop, the two fighters end up in the same place at the start of the scene and at the end of it, but you can smooth the program so it's hard to tell when the loop ends and begins. Anyone observing the scene for more than a few minutes almost always notices it looping. You're unable to alter the program after you create the illusion.

Any creature that touches any part of the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. If they interact with a portion of the illusion, they disbelieve only that portion. They disbelieve the entire scene only on a critical success.

Heightened (6th) Creatures or objects in your scene can speak. You must speak the specific lines for each actor when creating your program. The spell disguises your voice for each actor.

Heightened (8th) As the 6th-rank version, and the duration is unlimited.
cN0uSsE4bDqglpcP.name: Illusory Scene (Echo of the Past)

You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically, so you can use it to form a bridge or set of stairs, for example. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 14, and 50 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section of the wall can be moved through, but the rubble created from it is difficult terrain.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 15.

Radlight Cap.description:
The radlights caps that flourish in many parts of Nar-Voth look like softly glowing, halfling-sized toadstools: a relatively common sight in the Darklands. When radlight caps change color, however, their dangerous nature becomes evident. With each color change, the fungi gain a new set of stimuli that trigger their deadly spore clouds. While a field of blue mushrooms may have attacked noisy interlopers, when they shift to red they assault anyone who moves a muscle. Many Nar-Voth natives, even non-sentient ones, have learned the colors and corresponding behaviors that will see them safely through a field of radlight caps.

Red Light, Green Light

Ayindilar elves claim that they originally cultivated radlight caps as an advanced warning system against radiation, and that the fungus's other color changes are merely an unintended mutation. Regardless, their original function remains useful enough that the elves rarely eradicate growths of radlight caps. Rather, they teach this warning rhyme to those who must pass through a radlight forest:

Red light stop,
Yellow drop.
Green light rush,
Blue light hush.
Black for terror, black for flight,
For this way comes the sickness light.

  • Red A non-fungus creature within 30 feet takes an attack, move, or manipulate action that the radlight cap can detect.

  • Yellow A non-fungus creature within 30 feet ends their turn without being @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

At the start of each round, if a radlight cap is within 100 feet of an object or creature that emits radiation, the radlight cap's color changes to black. While black, the radlight cap loses its Radlight aura and can't take actions or reactions.

Shivver.description:
In some Darklands cultures, prisoners are routinely fleshwarped into grotesque shapes at the whims of their cruel captors. These unfortunate victims are dubbed "shivvers" after the thrill of horror they elicit and as a nod to one of the more infamous Darklands prisons. Once ordinary humanoids, shivvers now sport wriggling tentacles, insectile mandibles, and other bizarre "improvements." The agony these modifications cause is enough to drive many shivvers into murderous rages.

It's often said that encountering a fleshwarp is evidence there's an even greater monster nearby: the cruel being that tortured the fleshwarp into its distorted form. The Darklands are home to many such monsters, both the fleshwarps and their creators.

Fugitives of the Shiv

While some prisons pride themselves on being inescapable, the wardens of the Shiv once routinely released their more "artistically" fleshwarped captives before their sentences were fully served. The wardens believed that the products of their cruel punishments would inspire fear and obedience throughout the Darklands.

Sicklight Wisp.description:
The greenish pall that sicklight wisps cast over their surroundings causes creatures within it to sicken and die. Whereas the will-o'-wisps typically encountered on the surface feed on fear, sicklight wisps feast on the illness they spread, taking joy in robbing creatures of their vigor and health.

Though most commonly associated with the pit of Mobhad Leigh, sicklight wisps are occasionally encountered elsewhere in the Darklands. Wicked creatures sometimes employ the wisps to foil attempts at scrying on their subterranean lairs, as anyone who uses magic to spy upon a sicklight wisp risks having their mind irrevocably shattered.

Curse of the Infirm

In the Darklands, sicklight wisps are feared by both healers and the sick, because they're drawn to hospitals and other places of healing. Able to travel invisibly and evade scrying, the wisps slip into sickrooms, becoming briefly visible as they drain the remaining life from ailing victims. To protect against the wisps, some long-standing institutions of healing have taken to planting radlight caps around their facilities, since these otherwise dangerous mushrooms turn black in the presence of even an invisible sicklight wisp.

Slithering Snakes.description: A black, snake-shaped rune summons sinuous, shadowy serpents to grab and bite intruders throughout the room.
Slithering Snakes.hazardDisable: @Check[acrobatics|dc:31] (expert) to approach the desk without triggering the trap, followed by @Check[thievery|dc:33] (expert) to erase the rune; conversely, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (6th rank; counteract DC 31) to counteract the rune
Slithering Snakes.name: Slithering Snakes

Sorcerous Skull Swarm.description:
The act of creating a demilich sometimes goes horribly awry, leaving behind a shattered remnant of a once-mighty spellcaster constantly leaking eldritch energies. The ruined spirit animates a cloud of debased copies of itself, glittering with cracked crystals in crude imitation, and it hungers constantly for the magical energies denied it in its corrupted immortality.

Some of the spellcaster's personality remains in the swarm, albeit usually unnaturally split between the skulls. As a consequence, the skulls argue among themselves as warring parts of the personality clamor to be heard, resulting in the swarm's fractious, inconstant attitude.

A skull swarm is composed of reanimated masses of craniums and jawbones, forming a terrifying avalanche of undead fury. Most skull swarms are mindless, though some retain a vestige of wit, awareness, and even magical talents from life, culminating in a highly intelligent swarm mind.

NZUOo1WmtomF3Pyf.description: Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[5d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect] save).
NZUOo1WmtomF3Pyf.name: Swarming Gnaw

PtvDEVABQH9iJs6d.description: The sorcerous skull swarm saps magic from nearby creatures. Any creature with the ability to cast spells (including innate spells) in the swarm's space takes @Damage[15d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save); on a failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} on a critical failure).
PtvDEVABQH9iJs6d.name: Siphon Magic

QNcsHGzGsxzU10k0.description:

QNcsHGzGsxzU10k0.name: Consume Spell

XAyHusrI0x96dmIN.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).
XAyHusrI0x96dmIN.name: Truesight (Constant)

rREO3eXjpKJUOkJt.description: You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. Attempt a counteract check against the target. If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.
rREO3eXjpKJUOkJt.name: Dispel Magic (At Will)

vRBgSJWn6sIDkLoJ.description: When a sorcerous skull swarm is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it erupts in an explosion of foul energy and bone fragments in a @Template[burst|distance:30], dealing @Damage[3d12[piercing],3d12[void]|options:area-damage] (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect] save).
vRBgSJWn6sIDkLoJ.name: Boneshard Burst

jHh3abloQ4NLwChm.name: Disrupt Qi

m2OWS2mSoPSVPljv.description:
Setting right the injustice that led to Sourpuss's death allows him to move on to the afterlife.

When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.
m2OWS2mSoPSVPljv.name: (Ghost) Rejuvenation

Strangleroot.description:
In the shallowest parts of the Darklands, roots sometimes break through cavern ceilings, dangling from above like living stalactites. The most deep-seated of these roots belong to carnivorous trees that draw sustenance not only from the soil, but from the blood of the creatures that wander beneath them. When people on the surface encounter a tree whose leaves are an out-of-season autumnal red, they're likely unaware that, somewhere deep underground, the tree's roots have snared a hapless Darklands creature and are draining its blood.

Darklands inhabitants who live beneath strangleroot forests learn to keep their eyes on the ceiling, where strangleroot taproots lurk. They also watch for desiccated corpses, either strewn about the floor or suspended from the ceiling by hanging roots.

Slow Digestion

Strangleroots might strike with lightning speed, but they have the patience of a slow-growing tree. Once they have a victim trussed up tight, they rarely drain all its blood at once; rather, they do so over the course of hours or days. They accelerate their feeding only to kill a troublesome captive or to engorge themselves, lacing their meal's blood with a poisonous sap as a deterrent against hostile creatures.

23xepirBy9z5Voy4.description:
Requirements The strangleroot is blood engorged

Effect The strangleroot sprays sap-poisoned blood in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20]. Each creature in the emanation takes @Damage[6d10[poison]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save. Afterward, the strangleroot is no longer blood engorged.
23xepirBy9z5Voy4.name: Blood Spray

C8b4aT9N2T7dxUre.description:

Effect The strangleroot retracts its dangling roots into the ceiling or re-extends its roots. While retracted, the strangleroot can't be targeted by attacks or effects, and it can't take any action except to extend its roots, reappearing in another space within 15 feet of the space it left. If a creature digs through 1 foot of the earth and stone, it removed the earthen layer protecting the strangleroot; the strangleroot is no longer retracted and can't use Retract again.
C8b4aT9N2T7dxUre.name: Retract

EWiZ9UF5VvTbytHb.description:

The strangleroot regains HP equal to the bleed damage dealt and becomes blood engorged. The strangleroot doesn't gain Hit Points from draining a creature that's already drained, but the creature's drained value increases by 1, killing them when they reach @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 5}. A creature's drained condition decreases by 1 per hour.
EWiZ9UF5VvTbytHb.name: Drain Blood

QODyprpC7acUM5VY.name: Haul Up

xLV0213p3qKjh8IY.name: Blood Engorged

Strangleroot.name: Strangleroot

Tajatizt.description:
To outsiders, the eldritch emeritus looks something like a joke—a befuddled old scholar, their mind so stuffed with obscure theorems and abstract metaphysics that concerns about mere daily reality fade away. Those who know them, however, know that the eldritch emeritus wrote more treatises of spells than most wizards have had hot dinners, and if sufficiently annoyed, is entirely capable of providing a brief, thorough, and fatal demonstration.

True power comes from knowledge—the power to shape the growth of kingdoms by mere whispers, stay three steps ahead of adversaries, or even know which flora is best for creating untraceable poisons.

IaBbc8nFODNXPMYv.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).
IaBbc8nFODNXPMYv.name: Detect Magic

Lo2DPYR2SoThib5R.description:
You protect the target with a powerful, long-lasting energy barrier. The target gains resistance 5 to acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, and void damage.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.4Lo2qb5PmavSsLNk]{Spell Effect: Energy Aegis}

Heightened (9th) The resistances increase to 10.
Lo2DPYR2SoThib5R.name: Energy Aegis (Constant)

MwXOJ48WT9VVfogY.description:
Although not all wizards have gone through formal training, it's become tradition to enchant robes representing the arduous training required and festoon them with honors one has earned. Typically, an accolade robe is styled after a single wizard school, with appropriate colors and symbols. Wearing these robes grants a +2 item bonus to Arcana checks.

The pockets of the robe tie to an extradimensional space that can hold 1 Bulk of items, none of which can have greater than light Bulk. The items must be related to spellcasting and academics—spellbooks, scrolls, wands, scholarly journals, and other academic supplies the GM allows. These items do not count against your Bulk limit. You can Interact to retrieve or stow items normally.

Activate—Review 1 (concentrate, manipulate)

Effect You retrieve an item of your choice from the robe's storage, then Recall Knowledge.

Activate—Extra Credit F (concentrate)

Frequency once per day

Effect You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a school spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it is lost.

Craft Requirements You are a wizard of the associated school.
MwXOJ48WT9VVfogY.name: Somewhat Disheveled Accolade Robe

PI9aHlpQqd8iKdjA.description:

PI9aHlpQqd8iKdjA.name: Third Contingent Sequencer

YnLObWaGlgd2Jikj.description: If a reaction would disrupt the eldritch emeritus's spellcasting action, the eldritch emeritus attempts a @Check[flat|dc:15]. On a success, the action isn't disrupted
YnLObWaGlgd2Jikj.name: Steady Spellcasting

egSqxbVRYX5yASsk.description: A spellbook holds the written knowledge necessary to learn and prepare various spells, a necessity for wizards (who typically get one for free) and a useful luxury for other spellcasters looking to learn additional spells. Each spellbook can hold up to 100 spells. The Price listed is for a blank spellbook.
egSqxbVRYX5yASsk.name: Spellbook

fBxV4p1qSabmBC4c.description:
Trigger A creature casts a spell the eldritch emeritus has prepared.

Effect The emeritus expends a prepared spell to counter the triggering creature's casting of that same spell. The emeritus loses their spell slot as if they had cast the triggering spell. The emeritus then attempts to counteract the triggering spell.
fBxV4p1qSabmBC4c.name: Counterspell

fXYdE4H2dFgwfhBi.description:
1 to 3

Requirements The eldritch emeritus has seen a creature Cast a Spell of 7th rank or lower during the previous round, that spell takes between one and three actions to cast, and that spell is on the arcane spell list

Effect The eldritch emeritus mastered that spell 30 years ago, and is happy to show how a real master does it. The emeritus Casts the same Spell but heightened to 8th rank. Didactic Arcanism uses the same number of actions as the original spell took to cast.
fXYdE4H2dFgwfhBi.name: Didactic Arcanism

This staff resembles a blackened and burned length of ashen wood. You can Interact to touch the tip of this staff to a torch, tinder, or a flammable substance to ignite a flame.

Activate Cast a Spell

Effect You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

  • Cantrip @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6DfLZBl8wKIV03Iq]{Ignition}

  • 2nd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ZdHjnpEQJuqOYSG]{Floating Flame}
  • 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ZdHjnpEQJuqOYSG]{Floating Flame}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball}
  • 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.YrzBLPLd3r9m6t1p]{Fire Shield}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}
  • 5th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}

Craft Requirements Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.
nzOWjJtrOIzlzULZ.name: +2 Greater Striking Staff of Fire (Major)

zd3mZYO4fau9fU0h.description:
You shake the ground, topple creatures into fissures, and collapse structures. The GM might add additional effects in certain areas. Cliffs might collapse, causing creatures to fall, or a lake might drain as fissures open up below its surface, leaving a morass of quicksand.

  • Shaking Ground The ground is difficult terrain, and creatures on it take a -2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, AC, and skill checks. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.09rtx50laDw68FGT]{Spell Effect: Earthquake (Shaking Ground)}
  • Fissures Each creature on the ground must attempt a Reflex save at the start of its turn to keep its footing and avoid falling into 40-foot-deep fissures that open beneath it. The fissures are permanent, and their sides require successful @Check[athletics|dc:15|traits:action:climb] to Climb.
  • Collapse Structures and ceilings might collapse. The GM rolls a flat check for each (@Check[flat|dc:16] for a sturdy structure, @Check[flat|dc:14] for an average structure and most natural formations, @Check[flat|dc:9] for a shoddy structure, all adjusted higher or lower as the GM sees fit). A collapse deals 11d6 bludgeoning damage to each creature caught in it with a basic Reflex save. A creature falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} unless it critically succeeds and falls into a fissure if it critically fails.

Heightened (10th) You create a massive earthquake that can devastate a settlement. The range increases to half a mile and the area to a quarter-mile burst.
zd3mZYO4fau9fU0h.name: Earthquake

Tajatizt.name: Tajatizt

Telepathic Whispers.description: The spirits of the dead entice visitors with forbidden knowledge.
Telepathic Whispers.hazardDisable: @Check[occultism|dc:40] or @Check[religion|dc:40] (expert) to ward off the spirits' influence, @Check[intimidation|dc:42] (trained) to silence the whispers. A PC who brandishes the gaze of eternity gains a +2 item bonus to their checks. Three successes total are required to disable the haunt.
Telepathic Whispers.hazardReset: The hazard deactivates after 1 minute or after the spirits have answered three questions, whichever comes first. It resets after 24 hours.
Telepathic Whispers.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The spirits peer into the minds of up to three creatures in the area. Each creature attempts a @Check[will|dc:40|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save. On a failure, the target must choose to either divulge a closely guarded secret or take @Damage[(4d8+18)[mental]|options:area-damage] damage. On a critical success, the target can ask the haunt a question, which the spirits answer truthfully to the best of their ability.
Telepathic Whispers.name: Telepathic Whispers

5F2LyiH4JSIpkYPJ.description:
You create an illusion that causes the target to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise is typically good enough to hide their identity, but not to impersonate a specific individual. The spell changes their appearance and voice, but not mannerisms. You can change the appearance of its clothing and worn items, such as making its armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item removed from the creature returns to its true appearance.

Casting illusory disguise counts as setting up a disguise for the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} use of Deception; it ignores any circumstance penalties the target might take for disguising itself as a dissimilar creature, gives a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through the disguise, and lets the target add its level to such Deception checks even if untrained. You can Dismiss this spell.

Heightened (3rd) The target can appear as any creature of the same size, even a specific individual. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

Heightened (4th) You can target up to 10 willing creatures. If you target multiple creatures, you can choose a different disguise for each target, but none can impersonate a specific individual. You can Dismiss each disguise individually or all collectively.

Heightened (7th) As 4th, but you can choose disguises that impersonate specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to replicate its appearance, and must have heard its voice to replicate its voice.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.3Ktyd5F9lOPo4myk]{Spell Effect: Illusory Disguise}
5F2LyiH4JSIpkYPJ.name: Illusory Disguise (At Will)

8yjiPq56duywFZxd.description: The target's form appears blurry. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}. As the nature of this effect still leaves the target's location obvious, the target can't use this concealment to Hide or Sneak.
8yjiPq56duywFZxd.name: Blur (Self Only, At Will)

DyrMVf85ZqNuDoQz.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
DyrMVf85ZqNuDoQz.name: Truespeech (Constant)

R1QNkqz4NjdqK0fJ.description:
Whenever you speak or make any other sound vocally, you can make your vocalization seem to originate from somewhere else within 60 feet, and you can change that apparent location freely as you vocalize. Any creature that hears the sound can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) The spell's duration increases to 1 hour, and you can also change the tone, quality, and other aspects of your voice. Before a creature can attempt to disbelieve your illusion, it must actively attempt a Perception check or otherwise use actions to interact with the sound.
R1QNkqz4NjdqK0fJ.name: Ventriloquism (At Will)

VZoX1om80UduIVfW.description: Tenazki recovers slowly from injuries. When he takes physical damage from a critical hit, he gains @Damage[2d4[persistent,bleed]] damage. He takes a –2 circumstance penalty to flat checks to recover from persistent damage and saving throws against afflictions.
VZoX1om80UduIVfW.name: Thin of Blood

eCR1apfFRah9sypL.name: Religious Symbol of Abraxas

no0dNdeJRHQqIcGM.name: Potent Serpentfolk Venom

You channel void energy to harm the living or heal the undead. If the target is a living creature, you deal 1d8 void damage to it, and it gets a basic Fortitude save. If the target is a willing undead creature, you restore that amount of Hit Points. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines its targets, range, area, and other parameters.

1 The spell has a range of touch.

2 (concentrate) The spell has a range of 30 feet. If you're healing an undead creature, increase the Hit Points restored by 8.

3 (concentrate) You disperse void energy in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This targets all living and undead creatures in the area.

Heightened (+1) The amount of healing or damage increases by 1d8, and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8.
rPcqVgIZWZiwVLlh.name: Harm (At Will)

vkzdQ9lfFHqLGSax.description: Tenazki calls upon the power of Abraxus, briefly transforming the end of his whip into writhing viper. If Tenazki's next attack is to make a whip Strike, the target is also subjected to Potent Serpentfolk Venom.
vkzdQ9lfFHqLGSax.name: Biting Whip

Terror Glyphs.hazardDisable: @Check[acrobatics|dc:38] or @Check[athletics|dc:38] (expert) to move through the area before the glyph activates, @Check[arcana|dc:40] (expert) to unweave the glyph's animating magic, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 36)
Terror Glyphs.name: Terror Glyphs

1xEArAn6rJ5n51uv.description: The thash has Hardness 10 against damage from sources directly above it. Vault Lifter.description:
Vault lifters are sentient stone constructs roughly carved into the semblance of giant xiomorns. Each vault lifter is encircled by a spinning ring, called a rotor, which grants the lifter the ability to fly.

Xiomorns created vault lifters to help construct their vaults throughout the Plane of Earth and across the Universe. With the ability to airlift heavy burdens and possessed with enough intelligence to carry out complex instructions, vault lifters were valuable lieutenants in the xiomorns' vast terraforming projects. Vault lifters were intended to be more than simple laborers, however; they were also built as weapons of war. In combat, vault lifters spin their rotors into fearsome buzz saws capable of propelling them at high speeds and slicing foes in half.

Abandoned Guardians

While some vault lifters continue to serve living xiomorns, others have been left behind in long-abandoned locations. Over the years, many of these forgotten vault lifters have completed their assignments and deactivated themselves. Others continue to perform some unending task, such as "keep this area clean," "prevent unauthorized entry," or "I'll be back in a bit—wait for my return." After millennia spent in solitude, some abandoned vault lifters become fanatical about their final orders, spinning them into complex philosophical systems heavy with moral significance.

Vemerak.description:
A vemerak looks like a mishmash between a burrowing insect and a grotesque sea creature, stretched and warped to a titanic scale. When it first bursts from a half-buried hidey-hole or scuttles down a narrow tunnel, its form is obscured by a tangle of spidery legs and tentacles. Only when an unfortunate witness views the creature up close is the vemerak's immense, ant-like body revealed. At one end of the beast, glittering eyes blink above short, wriggling tentacles and serrated mouthparts, while three tail-like tentacles wave and slap at the other. Blue-green mold flakes from the vemerak's flanks, and wherever the mold lands, magic around it fades.

With its clicking pincers and corrosive bile, the vemerak is often mistaken for a mindless predator like a scorpion or spider, but it has enough wit to speak to its intended prey. A vemerak's words are often cruel, focused on the pain it plans to inflict on its victims.

Though most often encountered in the Darklands, in ages past vemeraks roamed Golarion's surface, leaving chaos and suffering in their wake. The creatures have even been encountered on other planets in Golarion's solar system, such as the distant Triaxus.

Rovagug's Pets

Though in its natural state a vemerak is hardly more intelligent than a predatory animal, its mind is linked to the urges and drives of the god Rovagug. When slaughter is in the offing, a vemerak becomes capable of laying traps with cunning and foresight, and its otherwise limited vocabulary grows poetic as it threatens foes with suffering and death. The farther a vemerak travels from Golarion's depths, the more tenuous its link to Rovagug becomes. Vemeraks found in the shallower parts of the Darklands are as mindless as cave worms or giant insects.

Xiomorn troopers are an elite military force formed from the ranks of xiomorn vault keepers. Armed with technology only they understand, xiomorn troopers hold the line against those who oppose the mysterious aims of the vault builders.

Many xiomorn troopers possess special training or equipment that helps them perform specific roles within their strike force. Comm troopers, for example, can communicate telepathically with their fellow troopers, while scout troopers surround themselves with fields of light-bending energy on their patrols. Yig.description:
To call Yig benign is perhaps too generous, but among the eldritch entities that comprise the Great Old Ones and Outer Gods, the word is indeed apropos. While those who worship Yig know that the patience of the so-called Father of Serpents is limited and expect no kindness from him, Yig nonetheless seeks vengeance against those who harm his beloved serpents—and sometimes his non-serpent worshippers as well.

Great Old Ones

Although Yig is one of the least powerful of the Great Old Ones, his might vastly outstrips that of most mortal creatures. He exists outside of the cycle of souls and is immortal—if a way exists that Yig can be permanently slain, none yet know it. Likewise, no one can say for certain where Yig's home world lies. Indeed, the Great Old One counts any world on which serpents might be found as his own.

Yig's Worshippers

Yig has worshippers on many worlds, and unlike most Great Old Ones, he sometimes takes notice of those who venerate him. He has even been known to reward his faithful from time to time—a trait not shared by the other Great Old Ones. Worship of Yig has long been a point of friction in sekmin society, where venerating deities other than Ydersius is often synonymous with treason. Additional information concerning Yig's worshippers, including his clerics, appears on pages 318–319 of Pathfinder Lost Omens Divine Mysteries.

Zyss Assassin.description:
Potential zyss assassins are selected from among the offspring of high-ranking sekmins and trained to remove threats both external and internal. In sekmin culture, to die at the hand of a zyss assassin is considered an honorable fate (though not one that's generally desired). Despite this elite status, the training zyss assassins must undergo is both rigorous and cruel. Zyss assassins train for years, learning to rely on no weapon other than those with which they were born, and submit to painful procedures to gain their most fearsome tool: their extraordinarily corrosive spit.

Although zyss assassins are perfectly happy to work alone, they're often deployed in groups of three or more. While one assailant wraps a target in their coils, their confederates strike with poisoned fangs. If their attack is successful, the target's corpse is dissolved with acid, leaving no trace behind.

Serpentfolk society is riddled with secret organizations, many of which preserve long-lost traditions from the height of the ancient sekmin empire. Exclusive orders of aapoph sovereign guards and zyss assassins, among others, trace their origins back millennia, training in the same techniques they employed in the days when mammalian humanoids were nothing but servants or prey.

Leave no Trace

Over the course of centuries, zyss assassins have carried out assignments for nearly every faction within sekmin culture. The common thread of these missions is that they each required plausible deniability. To that end, every zyss assassin is implanted with acid sacs harvested from a vemerak's stomach. Not only can a zyss use their corrosive spit to dissolve their victims, but when a zyss assassin dies, their body explodes in a burst of acidic sludge that leaves behind no evidence of their existence.
